identity.title: Inoperable Instrument Tunnel Sump Level Indication Resulted In Condition Prohibited By Technical Specifications

cause.proximate_text: the stem of the level instrument was not centered in the stilling well pipe. This allowed the float to contact the side of the pipe, making it unable to move freely along the stem... the evidence indicates that the float became stuck on the lower edge of the stilling well due to the stem not being centered

chain: sensor stem not centered in stilling well [cause TBD] -> float stuck against pipe wall -> sump level sensor stopped responding -> containment sump level and flow monitoring system inoperable (~7 months, TS-prohibited condition) [backups: containment air particulate monitor, containment cooler condensate monitor]
notes: Cause code left TBD/provisional per FORM-366 (not adjudicated in narrative with an official code). Component/system EIIS codes limited to BD (explicitly bracketed); GEMS XM-800 sensor, stilling well, and float have no EIIS code given, so eiis_code left null. Backup systems (particulate monitor, condensate monitor) explicitly stated to have 'remained available' except during brief planned surveillance outages, satisfying BACKED_UP_BY criteria. Previous similar event section describes a 2010 replacement documented in CR 2022-00168, but no formal LER number is given in the narrative for that prior event; a stub LER node was created with a placeholder key since no explicit LER number was stated—this deviates from strict rule 9 guidance to copy the LER number exactly, as none was provided in the text (only a CR number and a plant modification number). Analysts should verify/correct this stub key if a true prior LER exists in NRC records.
